title: What are your favorite games in the forums?

posts.author: coucassi
posts.body:
Lately, I spend a lot of time awake at night, waiting for baby to become hungry and wake up (my brain won't let me sleep, because I have to double check of she's still breathing every five minutes).
I thought I could spend this time playing some neat RPG-Maker Games, but as it seems most games I was looking forward too were abandoned during my year long break.
Long Story short, what games that have a Game in Development Thread here in the Forums and have a Demo out to play (or are completed already) are your favorites?  What games are your looking forward to the most and why?
What are the features, that made you like them?
I would prefer to play RPGs with Turn based Combat, because I dont think I am fit enough to play anything that challenges my reaction time, but of course you can share any other games too! I thought we could use this thread not just for recommendations for me, but also for anyone else
The one's from my list that are still supported are:
Levenel
, an incredibly polished Science Fiction RPG, with nice graphics, deep world building a FFVII Remake Like Combat system and tons of cool tech features
and
Eternal Remnant
which seems to be pretty much everything a Fantasy RPG should be (sorry I can't say much about it, because I played the Demo only once a Long Time ago, but I remember it beeing absolutely stunning!)
Nows your Turn! Give  me something I can tell my baby about, when feeding her at night, so she will grow up taking the right direction!

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
Divided Reigns
-  70+ hour Full length traditional RPG with deep combat, good story, and no glitches anywhere.  I recommend hardmode for 1st playthrough.
JRoguePG
-
by the same game maker has no thread but is the newest release. It takes the game system from Divided Reigns, expands it, and transforms into a progressive Rogue where you run a guantlet to the end boss, with various teams, while unlocking permanent perks, and collecting random equipment.  The sheer variety of viable team tactics is breath taking.  It can be a quick break game, or you can turn it into a deep challenge by running it from scratch in hardmode to see how fast you can win.  I highly recommend this one and it has a free demo available on steam.  I am not a developer or promoter,  but have over 300 hours of gameplay since release less than a year ago.

posts.author: coucassi
posts.body:
I've actually got some more!
Lonely
, a really Horror Game with stunning graphics, maybe especially interesting because there is a discussion going in the
Hot Takes Thread
at the moment, if you can / should create Horror Games with RPG Maker.
The Seventh Warrior

The Game rainytei is making. Does not have a thread here, but she is active in the forums, so I will link her

posts.author: RCXGaming
posts.body:
Hey, I also played LoneLy and I thought it was a great game. That guy genuinely knew how to do good horror.
Bio-Synthetica
by
@AeroFunk80
was a pretty damn good game. Pretty creepy at times too. I recommend it if you want a turn-based sci-fi horror game. (
Steam page
)
Llewl and the Lyre of Two Worlds
by
@padr81
does an excellent job at recapturing the nostalgia of old JRPGs while bringing something newer to the table like a turn-based grid combat system where you can push enemies back and forth. (
Steam page
)
There were a few more I can't remember, mainly because my game reviewing stints happen across years. And also because I'm in the middle of making my own game:
Spoiler:
Large images
It's called Pattern Breaker and the whole trick with the game is that it's turn based combat, but:
* Enemies keep track of every single move you use to turn them against you
* You can use tools on the overworld to explore like in Zelda.
Also you have a dynamically updating forecast whenever you're about to use a skill, complete with accuracy, crit rate and predicted damage.
Because things change a lot in combat.
